item.title: AMP Says Bonds No Longer a Hedge, Cuts From Some Pension Funds
item.description: AMP Ltd., one of Australia’s top asset managers, has ditched bonds from some of its retirement funds with sovereign debt no longer offering the diversification investors have relied on for decades as a ballast against stock volatility.

item.title: Takaichi Eyes India Ties as Relations With China Fray
item.description: Exchange rates of both Japan and India are under pressure.

item.title: MBK Partners Faces Sanctions Process in Homeplus Case, FSS Says
item.description: South Korea’s financial watchdog is moving ahead with sanctions against private equity firm MBK Partners Ltd. over issues related to its distressed portfolio company, retailer Homeplus Co.

item.title: Copper Climbs With Industrial Metals as Rate-Hike Prospects Fade
item.description: Copper rose with other industrial metals, supported by a weaker US dollar and reduced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in the coming months.

item.title: PBOC Cuts Bond Purchases in Sign of Wariness Over Yield Declines
item.description: China’s central bank trimmed its government bond purchases to the smallest in nine months in June, suggesting policymakers are turning cautious about potential further yield declines or excessive liquidity.

item.title: China Services Gauge Fares Better Than Forecast Despite Slip
item.description: China’s services activity eased less than expected in June, a private survey showed, adding to signs that the country’s economic momentum is picking up.

item.title: Vietnam Growth Tops Estimates Despite Trade Risks, Oil Shock
item.description: Vietnam’s economic growth beat estimates in the second quarter, while trade grew faster than expected in June and inflation slowed, as one of Asia’s fastest-growing economies continues to defy tariff risks and higher energy prices.

item.title: Renk Group Nears Deal to Buy UK’s David Brown Defence
item.description: Industrial machinery maker Renk Group AG is nearing a deal to acquire privately held David Brown Defence, in a move that gives it more exposure to the naval sector, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Katayama Repeats Ready to Act on Yen, in Touch With US
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama repeated that she and her colleagues can take appropriate action on foreign exchange at any time, as market participants grow increasingly alert to the possibility of currency intervention.

item.title: Japan Cuts Gas in Favor of Coal as Hormuz Disruption Chokes LNG
item.description: Japan sharply reduced natural gas-fired power generation last month, instead relying more on coal, as disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz tightened supplies of the cleaner-burning fuel.

item.title: India’s Space Industry Hunts for Its SpaceX Moment
item.description: India’s attempt to fire up its fledgling private space program is showing early signs of success.

item.title: Gold Rises Toward $4,200 as Weak Jobs Data Lowers Rate-Hike Odds
item.description: Gold extended two days of gains after weak US jobs data reduced the chances of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates this year to tackle inflation.

item.title: China Tech’s Deepening Valuation Slump Fails to Win Back Buyers
item.description: The selloff in China’s biggest internet firms has driven some valuations to record lows but investors say a recovery still looks a way off given the many headwinds they face.

item.title: Chip Industry Urges US to Avoid Moves That Distort Memory Market
item.description: Government attempts to address the global memory chip shortage by influencing prices or production capacity would worsen a historic squeeze on supply driven by the artificial intelligence boom, a semiconductor industry group warned the Trump administration.

item.title: Kioxia Ships Samples of New Flash Memory for AI Data Centers
item.description: Kioxia Holdings Corp. has started shipping samples of its next-generation flash memory chips to AI data center operators, seeking to gain ground in the lucrative business against rivals.

item.title: Trump Thinks Musk Will Donate SpaceX Stock to Trump Accounts
item.description: President Donald Trump said he thinks Elon Musk will donate SpaceX stock to the Trump accounts initiative, following other technology executives who have embraced the new investment vehicles for children.

item.title: Booming AI Chip Trade Seals Hong Kong’s Role as Gateway to China
item.description: Hong Kong has become a vital conduit for high-tech products moving in and out of China, emerging as one node in a $2 trillion network of Asian trade fueled by a global boom in artificial intelligence.

item.title: Japan’s Convertible Bonds Regain Favor as Rates Continue to Rise
item.description: Japanese companies have sold the highest amount of convertible bonds in more than two decades in the first half, turning to the cheaper financing alternative as interest rates continue to climb.

item.title: China Quant Funds Draw Billions as AI Trounces Human Traders
item.description: Quant funds in China have become so popular that they are being deluged with investors’ money.

item.title: Trump Says He Wants AI Guardrails, But ‘As Little as Possible’
item.description: President Donald Trump said he sees the need for some standards on artificial intelligence technology, but wants to avoid burdensome restrictions that may hamper American companies competing with China.

item.title: Asian Stocks to Fall a Second Day on Tech Worries: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were set to decline for a second session as investors continued to rotate out of technology shares on concerns that the artificial intelligence-fueled rally has run ahead of itself.

item.title: Oil Steadies as More Supply Flows Through Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Oil steadied as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz increased further, adding to a gush of near-term supply while talks between the US and Iran continue.

item.title: Trump Says Fed’s Warsh Faces Board That’s a ‘Bit Hostile’
item.description: President Donald Trump said Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh may not be able to compel his colleagues on the central bank to do what the new chair wants on monetary policy.

item.title: Crusoe in Talks to Raise $3 Billion in Round That May Triple Firm’s Value
item.description: Crusoe, the data center upstart with contracts to supply AI computing power for the likes of Meta Platforms Inc. and Oracle Corp., is in talks to raise about $3 billion in a funding round that may triple the company’s valuation, people familiar with the situation said.

item.title: Canada, Philippines Agree to Sign Trade Deal This Year, Grow Defense Ties
item.description: Canada and the Philippines plan to finalize a free trade agreement this year, and signed agreements to deepen cooperation on energy, defense, labor and migration, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday.

item.title: 【今朝の5本】仕事を始める前に読んでおきたい厳選ニュース
item.description: ​米雇用統計、海峡通航料、インサイダー疑惑、AIチップ製造パートナー、キーウ攻撃

item.title: South Korea Opens 24-Hour Won Trading at a Fraught Moment
item.description: Deep inside a government complex in Sejong, about two hours from Seoul, a room known as “the box” is ground zero for South Korea’s currency anxieties.

item.title: World’s Worst-Performing Exchange ASX Bets on Outsider for Pivot
item.description: When Anthony Attia takes the helm at Australia’s ASX Ltd., the world’s worst-performing stock exchange operator, he’ll need to launch straight into a battle to win over regulators and investors.

item.title: Los conciertos de Bad Bunny muestran cómo la migración latina está impulsando la economía de España
item.description: En los últimos tres años, el país ha acogido a más de tres millones de personas, muchas de ellas procedentes de América Latina. Estas personas han contribuido a convertir a España en la economía de la eurozona de más rápido crecimiento.

item.title: Wall Street Bets Rallying Markets Will Absorb Every Market Blow
item.description: Wall Street is kicking off the second half of 2026 with fresh conviction: shrugging off one shock after another, markets are set to grind even higher.
